description: KV-cache index, KV-events subscriber and tokenization health for the llm-d precise prefix-cache pipeline.

options.content:
# KV-Cache Index

Operational view of the precise prefix-cache pipeline embedded in the EPP: the KV-block index, the KV-events subscribers that feed it, and the tokenization step in front of it. The `llm_d_epp_kv_cache_index_*` panels stay at zero unless the `precise-prefix-cache-producer` sets `indexerConfig.kvBlockIndexConfig.enableMetrics: true`. Where EPP replicas keep separate state (KV-events subscribers, index, latency), panels split by replica (`pod`) so one broken replica stays visible. Metric definitions: [pkg/kvcache/metrics](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/tree/main/pkg/kvcache/metrics).

panels.title: Predicted Hit Rate
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens the precise producer predicted the chosen endpoint already holds, over the dashboard's time range. Speculative entries keep repeated prefixes hitting even without KV events, so this is not a stream-health signal.

panels.title: Index Lookups / s
panels.description: Rate of KV-block index Lookup calls.

panels.title: Replicas w/o KV Events
panels.description: EPP replicas that scored requests (the precise producer recorded prompts) in the last 10 minutes but received no KV events at all in that time: the replica's whole stream is dead or never connected, even though speculative entries keep its admissions up. Idle replicas are not counted. It is per replica: one dead stream among several model servers does not trip it, but shows in Messages Received by Pod as a line dropping to 0. vLLM sends an event only when a block fills, so a workload that only reuses already-cached prefixes for 10 minutes can also trip it. It can read 1 briefly while a new replica receives its first events.

targets.expr: count((sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_prefix_prompt_tokens_count{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", plugin_type="precise-prefix-cache-producer"}[10m])) > 0) unless on (namespace, pod) (sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_messages_received_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[10m])) > 0)) or vector(0)

panels.title: Event Backlog
panels.description: Most KV-event messages queued across any EPP replica's event-pool worker shards. A sustained backlog means the index lags behind the model servers; raise kvEventsConfig.concurrency if it stays high.

panels.title: Mean Lookup Latency
panels.description: Mean duration of index Lookup and WalkKeys calls on the slowest EPP replica. Lookups run on the request path. A mean is shown because the histogram's lowest bucket is 5ms, so sub-5ms quantiles are interpolated rather than measured.

targets.expr: max(sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_index_lookup_latency_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_index_lookup_latency_seconds_count{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Active Subscribers
panels.description: ZMQ subscribers managed by the EPP replica with the fewest, including subscribers retrying a failed connection. With pod discovery each replica subscribes to every model server pod its podLabelSelector matches (all pods by default), so this should match that count; in single-socket mode (zmqEndpoint) it is 1. 0 means that replica cannot receive KV events.

panels.title: Admissions vs Evictions
panels.description: Blocks written to and removed from each EPP replica's index per second. Both include speculative entries: with speculativeIndexing on (the precise guide's default), each routing decision seeds entries that expire after speculativeTTL, so these rates follow request volume and stay non-zero even when no KV events arrive. Cache resets (AllBlocksCleared) remove a pod's blocks without counting as evictions. Use the KV-Events Subscribers row for stream health.

panels.title: Lookup Rate by EPP Replica
panels.description: Index Lookup calls per second, per EPP pod.

panels.title: Predicted Prefix Hit Rate
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens each EPP replica's precise producer predicted the chosen endpoint holds in its prefix cache, next to the model servers' measured prefix-cache hit rate per namespace (vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total / vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total, also a share of prompt tokens). With a complete index the lines track each other. If the model servers' line is clearly higher than a replica's, that replica's index is missing blocks: check the KV-Events Subscribers row. If both are low, the workload shares little prefix. The comparison does not hold with prefill/decode disaggregation (decode pods' queries dilute the model-server line) or when the index tracks a CPU or offload tier (vLLM's counter covers only the GPU prefix cache); there the model-server line can sit below the router's even with an incomplete index. A router line alone is not a stream-health signal, because speculative entries keep repeated prefixes hitting without KV events. The model-server line includes every vLLM pool in the namespace, needs the model servers to be scraped, and is absent for SGLang.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_prefix_predicted_cached_tokens_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", plugin_type="precise-prefix-cache-producer"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_prefix_prompt_tokens_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", plugin_type="precise-prefix-cache-producer"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Matched Prefix Blocks per Lookup
panels.description: Average length of the longest contiguous prefix chain a single pod holds, per lookup, per EPP replica. This counts blocks, so it is not a 0-1 hit rate.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_index_lookup_hits_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_index_lookup_requests_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Prompt vs Predicted-Cached Tokens
panels.description: Prompt tokens per second scored by the precise producer, and the portion predicted to be served from the chosen endpoint's prefix cache.

panels.title: Index Lookup Latency
panels.description: Duration of index Lookup and WalkKeys calls per EPP replica, including WalkKeys callbacks. The histogram uses Prometheus default buckets, whose lowest bound is 5ms, so quantiles below 5ms are interpolated within that bucket rather than measured. P99 catches tails above 5ms; below that, read the exact mean.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_index_lookup_latency_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_index_lookup_latency_seconds_count{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Render Latency (token-producer)
panels.description: Duration of successful token-producer render calls per EPP replica: the call to vLLM's render endpoint (a model server or a standalone render service) that tokenizes each prompt before the index lookup. Buckets run from 5ms to 60s, so quantiles below 5ms are interpolated; the mean is exact. Only the vllm render backend records this: it stays empty with the estimate backend or when requests arrive already tokenized (for example from the vLLM gRPC parser). Warmup renders at startup are not counted. Only EPP replicas running the precise producer are shown.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_token_producer_render_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", result="success"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (namespace, pod) llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_token_producer_render_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", result="success"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (namespace, pod) llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}))

sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_token_producer_render_duration_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", result="success"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (namespace, pod) llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) / sum by (pod) (rate(llm_d_epp_token_producer_render_duration_seconds_count{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", result="success"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (namespace, pod) llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Render Failures
panels.description: Failed token-producer render calls per second, by EPP replica and reason (timeout, status, connection, decode, no_endpoints, other). A failed render leaves the request without tokens, so the precise producer cannot score it against the index. status counts non-2xx responses from the render endpoint, including requests vLLM rejects, such as prompts longer than the model's context. Calls canceled because the client went away are not counted. Only EPP replicas running the precise producer are shown.

targets.expr: sum by (pod, reason) (rate(llm_d_epp_token_producer_render_failures_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (namespace, pod) llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Precise Producer Time by Extension Point
panels.description: P99 and mean time, per EPP replica, the precise-prefix-cache-producer spends in each extension point (scoring-path lookup, speculative indexing on PreRequest). llm_d_epp_plugin_duration_seconds tops out at a 100ms bucket, so P99 caps there; the mean is exact.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, pod, extension_point) (rate(llm_d_epp_plugin_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", plugin_type="precise-prefix-cache-producer"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum by (pod, extension_point) (rate(llm_d_epp_plugin_duration_seconds_sum{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", plugin_type="precise-prefix-cache-producer"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod, extension_point) (rate(llm_d_epp_plugin_duration_seconds_count{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", plugin_type="precise-prefix-cache-producer"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Messages Received by Pod
panels.description: KV-event messages received per second, per model server pod (pod_identifier) and EPP replica (pod). Every replica keeps its own subscriber to every model server, so a stream that stops shows as one line at 0 instead of a dip in a combined total. A stream that has not delivered any event since the EPP started has no line at all, because the counter is created on the first message: compare the lines per replica with Active Subscribers. A replica that receives no events at all is flagged by Replicas w/o KV Events.

panels.title: Subscriber Reconnections
panels.description: Reconnection attempts per second, per model server pod and EPP replica. A sustained rate means the EPP keeps losing that pod's event stream.

panels.title: ZMQ Errors
panels.description: ZMQ subscriber errors per second by model server pod, EPP replica and failed operation (bind, connect, subscribe, recv, snapshot, replay-*).

panels.title: Event Pool Backlog
panels.description: Messages queued across all event-pool worker shards, and the number of shards. A sustained backlog means the index lags behind the model servers; raise kvEventsConfig.concurrency.

panels.title: Removal Dedup
panels.description: Block hashes whose removal the dedup filter suppressed (still referenced elsewhere) vs forwarded to the index as evictions. Shown per EPP replica.

panels.title: Skipped Events
panels.description: Store and removal events skipped before prefix indexing, by EPP replica, cache kind and reason.

panels.title: Scrape Up
panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape each EPP replica hosting the index. A replica stays listed for an hour after it stops exporting KV-cache metrics, so a failing scrape shows as 0 instead of disappearing. A replica that has not exported KV-cache metrics at all in the last hour, such as one crash-looping since creation, cannot be identified and is not shown.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (up{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} and on (namespace, pod, container) max_over_time(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h]))

panels.title: EPP Resident Memory
panels.description: Resident memory of each EPP replica. With the in-memory index backend, index size shows up here.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (process_resident_memory_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} and on (namespace, pod, container) llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: EPP Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines per EPP replica. Each KV-events subscriber runs its own goroutine, so this tracks subscriber count plus request load.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (go_goroutines{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} and on (namespace, pod, container) llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: EPP Restarts
panels.description: Restarts over the last hour of the container serving the EPP metrics, per replica (requires kube-state-metrics). A restart empties the in-memory index; sidecar restarts, such as the proxy's, do not and are excluded. Counts are rounded, because increase() extrapolates. A pod replaced by a new one (rollout, eviction) shows as a new line rather than a restart, and also starts with an empty index. Crash-looping replicas stay listed for an hour after they stop exporting KV-cache metrics. A replica that has not exported KV-cache metrics at all in the last hour, such as one crash-looping since creation, cannot be identified and is not shown.

targets.expr: round(sum by (pod) (max by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) and on (namespace, pod, container) max_over_time(llm_d_epp_kv_cache_events_pool_capacity{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])))

title: llm-d KV-Cache Index
